system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: Conjunctive-query equivalence of schema mappings
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Logical, data-exchange and CQ equivalence and their hierarchy. Covers collapse for st-tgd mappings, strictness with target constraints or SO tgds, and decidability boundaries.

ATOMS:
- CS-DB-C06-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: Two schema mappings $\mathcal{M}=(S,T,\Sigma)$ and $\mathcal{M}'=(S,T,\Sigma')$ are conjunctive-query equivalent if, for every source instance $I$ and every conjunctive query $q$, either $Sol(I,\mathcal{M})=Sol(I,\mathcal{M}')=\emptyset$ or $cert(q,I,\mathcal{M})=cert(q,I,\mathcal{M}')$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0115-s14] ▶Deﬁnition 6. [9] Let M = (S, T, Σ) and M′ = (S, T, Σ′) be two schema mappings.
    [CS-DB-p0115-s15] M and M′ are conjunctive-query equivalent, if for every source instance I and every conjunctive query q, either Sol(I, M) = Sol(I, M′) = ∅or
    [CS-DB-p0115-s16] cert(q, I, M) = cert(q, I, M′)
- CS-DB-C06-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: Assume $\mathrm{Sol}(I,M)\neq\emptyset$ implies $\mathrm{UnivSol}(I,M)\neq\emptyset$. Then $M$ and $M'$ are CQ-equivalent if, for every source instance $I$, either both have no solutions or $\mathrm{core}(I,M)=\mathrm{core}(I,M')$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0115-s24] ▶Proposition 7. [9] Let M = (S, T, Σ) and M′ = (S, T, Σ′) be two schema mappings such that the following holds.
    [CS-DB-p0115-s25] Sol(I, M)̸ = ∅ implies UnivSol(I, M)̸ = ∅
    [CS-DB-p0115-s26] M and M′ are conjunctive-query equivalent, if for every source instance I, either Sol(I, M) = Sol(I, M′) = ∅or
    [CS-DB-p0115-s27] ◀ core(I, M) = core(I, M′)
- CS-DB-C06-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: Two schema mappings can be CQ-equivalent for one of two reasons: both have no solutions for a source instance, or both have solutions and their certain answers to conjunctive queries coincide.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0115-s18] By this deﬁnition, there can be two reasons for schema mappings to be CQ-equivalent.
    [CS-DB-p0115-s19] The ﬁrst is that both schema mappings could have no solutions at all.
    [CS-DB-p0115-s21] The other case is of course that there are solutions to both schema mappings, and the certain answers to queries against them coincide.
- CS-DB-C06-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: For schema mappings based on s-t tgds, logical, DE- and CQ-equivalence coincide. These mappings are preserved under target homomorphisms and have a universal solution whenever a solution exists, and for such mappings the three notions are equivalent.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0126-s07] ▶Proposition 30. [9] If M and M′ are both preserved under target homomorphisms, and both have that Sol(I, M)̸ = ∅implies UnivSol(I, M)̸ = ∅for all I then M ≡log M′ iﬀM ≡DE M′ iﬀM ≡CQ M′. ◀
    [CS-DB-p0126-s08] From this, since the properties hold for s-t tgds, we have that the three notions of logical-, DE- and CQ-equivalence coincide for mappings based on s-t tgds.
- CS-DB-C06-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: If $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}'$ both have all the universal solutions, then $\mathcal{M}\equiv_{CQ}\mathcal{M}'$ implies $\mathcal{M}\equiv_{DE}\mathcal{M}'$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0125-s29] ▶Proposition 28. [9] If M and M′ have all the universal solutions, then M ≡CQ M′ implies M ≡DE M′. ◀
- CS-DB-C06-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: For schema mappings based on s-t tgds, logical equivalence, DE-equivalence and CQ-equivalence coincide.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0126-s08] From this, since the properties hold for s-t tgds, we have that the three notions of logical-, DE- and CQ-equivalence coincide for mappings based on s-t tgds.
- CS-DB-C06-S2-04 | S2
  ATOM: Logical equivalence, DE-equivalence and CQ-equivalence form a hierarchy: $\mathcal M\equiv_{log}\mathcal M'\Rightarrow\mathcal M\equiv_{DE}\mathcal M'\Rightarrow\mathcal M\equiv_{CQ}\mathcal M'$. This makes CQ-equivalence the weakest of the three notions.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0125-s04] Let us ﬁrst summarize what we have seen earlier in Section 3 when we introduced logical equivalence, DE-equivalence and CQ-equivalence: Logical equivalence, DE-equivalence and CQ-equivalence form a hierarchy (Proposition 8): M ≡log M′ ⇒M ≡DE M′ ⇒M ≡CQ M′.
- CS-DB-C06-S2-05 | S2
  ATOM: Logical equivalence, DE-equivalence and CQ-equivalence form a hierarchy: $M\equiv_{log}M'\Rightarrow M\equiv_{DE}M'\Rightarrow M\equiv_{CQ}M'$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0125-s04] Let us ﬁrst summarize what we have seen earlier in Section 3 when we introduced logical equivalence, DE-equivalence and CQ-equivalence: Logical equivalence, DE-equivalence and CQ-equivalence form a hierarchy (Proposition 8): M ≡log M′ ⇒M ≡DE M′ ⇒M ≡CQ M′.
- CS-DB-C06-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: CQ-equivalence is undecidable for schema mappings based on s-t tgds and a weakly acyclic set of target tgds, even for copy s-t tgds and full target tgds.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0126-s20] ▶Theorem 32. [9] Given two schema mappings M and M′ based on s-t tgds and a weakly acyclic set of target tgds it is decidable whether M ≡log M′ it is undecidable whether M ≡CQ M′
    [CS-DB-p0126-s21] The undecidability results holds even for copy s-t tgds and full target tgds. ◀
- CS-DB-C06-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: For schema mappings based on s-t tgds and target tgds, logical, DE- and CQ-equivalence are three distinct notions, so the hierarchy is proper.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0125-s05] For schema mappings based on s-t tgds and target tgds, all three notions are distinct (through Examples 3 and 5 in Section 3).
- CS-DB-C06-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: For schema mappings based on s-t tgds and a weakly acyclic set of target tgds, it is undecidable whether $\mathcal{M}\equiv_{CQ}\mathcal{M}'$. This holds even for copy s-t tgds and full target tgds.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0126-s20] ▶Theorem 32. [9] Given two schema mappings M and M′ based on s-t tgds and a weakly acyclic set of target tgds it is decidable whether M ≡log M′ it is undecidable whether M ≡CQ M′
    [CS-DB-p0126-s21] The undecidability results holds even for copy s-t tgds and full target tgds. ◀
